name: Half Guard Knee Shield
description: Use the knee shield (Z-guard) to create distance, win the underhook battle, and transition to sweeps, wrestle-ups, or submissions.
shortInstruction: Knee in their hip, frame on their head, win the underhook — knee shield is the control position of bottom half guard.
summary: The knee shield (also called Z-guard) is the most stable position in bottom half guard. Your nearside knee is inserted between your chest and their hip, creating a frame that prevents them from applying chest pressure. From here, you can fight for the underhook, create distance, and attack with sweeps (deep half, waiter), submissions (kimura), or wrestle-ups. If you lose the knee shield, you get flattened — so protecting it is your number one priority.
whyItWorks: The knee shield creates a structural frame that prevents chest-to-chest pressure — without pressure, they cannot pass.
It allows you to fight for the underhook from a safe distance, rather than getting flattened and smashed.
The knee shield can be extended to create space or retracted to close distance for sweeps.
Danaher principle: distance is safety in bottom half guard — the knee shield is your distance tool.
commonMistakes: Letting them push your knee shield to the side or flatten it against your chest.
Fighting for the underhook with a straight arm — you will lose every time.
Holding the knee shield too long without attacking — it is a transitional control position, not a resting position.
Letting them grab your collar or head to neutralize the shield — hand fight to strip these grips.
coachingCues: Knee in the hip, not the ribs.
Win the underhook or die trying.
Frame first, fight second — your knee shield is your frame.
When you feel their weight lift, that's your attack moment.
safetySummary: Keep your knee shield active — if it gets flattened, you are exposed to heavy chest pressure.
Protect your neck from crossfaces by keeping your head tight to their body, not exposed.
When they drive forward, do not brace with a straight arm — bend your elbow to protect the joint.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The knee shield (Z-guard) is a structural frame that prevents chest-to-chest pressure in bottom half guard. It is a transitional control position — you must attack (sweep, wrestle-up, or submission) rather than holding it passively.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent drives forward with chest pressure
decisionTree.action: Accept the pressure and enter deep half guard → waiter sweep. Their forward momentum feeds directly into the sweep. Do not resist the pressure — redirect it.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent postures up and lifts their weight
decisionTree.action: Technical stand-up → wrestle-up. The moment their weight lifts is your attack window. Stand up facing them, not turning away.
Kimura trap → sweep or submission. The reach across exposes their arm — capture the wrist and drive the kimura grip across their back.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent pushes your knee shield to the side
decisionTree.action: Extend your leg to push them away and re-frame the shield. If they flatten it against your chest, your underhook is the problem — fight harder for the underhook.
You cannot stay in knee shield without the underhook. Transition to deep half guard or recover to full guard. Do not stay flattened in bottom half.

exitStrategies: If the opponent passes your knee shield, you waited too long to attack — sweep or wrestle up sooner.
If you cannot get the underhook, use a collar tie or wrist grip to control their posture as an alternative.
The kimura from knee shield is one of the highest percentage no-gi submissions — bait the crossface to enter it.

moneyDetails: Your knee must be framed against their hip, not their stomach — hip control prevents them from stepping over the shield.
The underhook fight is won with your head: drive your head into their chest to create the space for your underhook.
When they try to flatten your shield, extend your leg to push them away — then attack before they recover.
The kimura from knee shield is one of the highest percentage submissions in no-gi half guard — bait the crossface to enter it.
nextStep: After knee shield control, learn the deep half sweep and kimura from half guard to chain with your attacks.
fixItFast: Knee shield getting flattened? Extend your leg to push them away and re-frame.
Can't get the underhook? Use a collar tie or wrist grip instead to control their posture.
They keep passing? Your knee shield is too loose — bring it tighter against your chest.
